stories.title: Charlotte nonprofits brace for summer hunger surge
stories.summary_or_snippet: Axios Charlotte reported that Charlotte nonprofits are preparing for a summer hunger spike as school meals end, Nourish Up serves about 12,000 households each month, and SNAP changes add pressure for families.
stories.evidence_text: Axios Charlotte reported that Charlotte nonprofits are preparing for a summer hunger spike as school meals end. Nourish Up serves about 12,000 households each month. About 68,000 Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools students receive free meals during the school year, and the group says it needs more delivery drivers as summer demand rises and SNAP eligibility changes add pressure for families.
stories.pressure_reason: matched child meal gap; school meals ending and SNAP changes increase summer hunger pressure
stories.pressure_summary: Charlotte nonprofits are preparing for summer hunger as school meals end, Nourish Up serves roughly 12,000 households a month, and SNAP changes add pressure for families.
stories.claim_supported: Charlotte nonprofits are preparing for summer hunger as school meals end, Nourish Up serves roughly 12,000 households a month, and SNAP changes add pressure for families.
stories.limitations: The source documents summer meal strain, but it does not prove a statewide trend.
